title.value: ASHA: Assistive Teleoperation via Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning
title.justification: The provided paper information includes the title, which is important to identify the specific focus and contribution of the paper.
title.quote: ASHA: Assistive Teleoperation via Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning

extractions.description: The paper introduces a hierarchical reinforcement learning approach called ASHA for assistive teleoperation, which adapts a user interface to infer actions from high-dimensional, noisy inputs like gaze from webcam images. It focuses on optimizing user feedback to guide a robot through tasks such as flipping light switches, opening doors, and rotating valves using gaze input to control a robotic arm.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on developing a human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning method for robotic teleoperation, which while innovative, does not directly target climate or ecological sustainability issues. The main focus is on enhancing human-computer interaction for assistive technologies.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Building assistive interfaces for controlling robots through arbitrary, high-dimensional, noisy inputs (e.g., webcam images of eye gaze) can be challenging, especially when it involves inferring the user’s desired action in the absence of a natural ‘default’ interface.

primary_category.justification: The paper's focus on assistive teleoperation and human-robot interfaces does not directly align with any specified categories in climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: In this paper, we focus on the problem of efficiently training an interface to infer the user’s desired action (e.g., robot arm motion) from an arbitrary, high-dimensional, noisy control input (e.g., webcam image of eye gaze).

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary sustainable development themes addressed as the primary focus is on assistive technology and reinforcement learning for improving teleoperation interfaces.
secondary_categories.quote: Shared-control teleoperation interfaces can help users control systems like robotic arms and wheelchairs more effectively.

primary_sub_category.justification: The subcategories applicable to climate or ecological sustainability are not relevant to this paper focused on assistive robotics.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our adaptive interface observes the user’s input, takes an action, receives a sparse, binary reward signal from the user at the end of each episode that indicates task success or failure, and learns to optimize this feedback.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: As the paper does not cover any areas pertaining to ecological or climate sustainability, there are no applicable sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: To run ablation experiments at a scale that would be impractical in a user study, we simulate user input x ∈ R^3 as the 3D position of the target switch or bottle with i.i.d. isotropic Gaussian noise added at each timestep.

applications.justification: The paper focuses on human-in-the-loop learning for assistive technologies, not on applications relevant to sustainable development.
applications.quote: The main challenge is that, due to the sparsity of rewards, it can require a large amount of training data, which may be impractical for an individual user operating a physical robot.

new_primary_category.justification: Given the existing categories, the paper does not introduce a new perspective that fits within the climate or ecological sustainability framework.
new_primary_category.quote: We primarily evaluate ASHA through a user study with 12 participants who use a webcam and their eye gaze to perform tasks in three simulated manipulation domains: flipping light switches, opening a shelf door to reach objects inside, and rotating a valve.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fit existing sub-categories relevant to sustainable development nor does it propose a novel area under this context.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Learning efficiently from successes in hindsight. Instead of simply imitating a successful trajectory, we imitate an optimal policy conditioned on task information extracted from the successful trajectory.
